Unclear: the chordoma rule counts any paper mentioning chordoma in its abstract, so a hemangioma case report that lists chordoma only in its differential was posted; say if that bar should be higher.

The Tier 2 limit of 10 and the preprint limit of 10 were both reached, so several on-topic experimental papers were left out.

notes: The bioRxiv connector returned HTTP 500 errors on many calls (search_preprints and get_preprint); I retried until each shortlisted DOI and each category/day range returned. Pages came back 30 at a time rather than 100 and paging by cursor 30/60 worked, so the README step 3 rule 'stop when a page has fewer than 100 results' does not apply to this connector.
Preprints dated 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08 were sparse in the listings, so the last two days may be under-covered.
No Figure 1 downloads: PubMed lists the three featured Nature papers as 'The Author(s)' with no open licence, so all three pictures are hand-drawn illustrations.

Chordoma rule: the one chordoma post is a clival chondrosarcoma case report that only mentions chordoma as the initial suspected diagnosis; it counts under the 'mentions chordoma in the abstract' rule.
Several preprints in the listings are revisions (v2, v3) of older DOIs; none of the DOIs had been posted before, so they were treated as new.

notes: bioRxiv search_preprints returned only 13-30 results per page for category filters even with limit=100, so the README rule 'stop when a page returns fewer than 100' would have stopped far too early. I kept paging until a page came back empty, and also re-queried narrower date windows (2 to 6 Oct, 3 to 6 Oct) because the first 7-day query only reached about 1 to 2 October for genomics, cancer biology and genetics. Coverage of those categories for 2 to 6 October rests on the narrower queries.
The first PubMed query for search 4 hit a rate limit and was retried successfully. get_article_metadata returns at most 20 papers per call, so metadata was fetched in batches.
Three Nat Commun papers have PubMed publication dates of 3 September but were added to PubMed this week (entry date), so they were treated as new.
Featured pictures are hand-drawn illustrations; Figure 1 was not downloaded because the tools in this session cannot fetch full-text figures, and the licences were not confirmed as CC BY.

Nature (SynthIDBio watermarking of AI proteins) and the UK Biobank fluid-intelligence imputation paper were posted under the rule that Tier 1 journals post every purely computational biology paper, although protein design and psychiatric genetics are otherwise outside the interest list.

README says the featured row should come from this run's Tier 1 research papers; I picked the three best matches (RovHer, CCI-seq, mistranslation) rather than the two purely computational ones that were off-topic.

No Figure 1 was reused: none of the three featured papers is open access (PubMed copyright status: all rights reserved or exclusive licence), so three illustrations were drawn by hand.
Revised preprints of older DOIs (2022-2025) whose DOI had never been posted were treated as new, per the README; their titles follow the latest version in the listing.
The 'Computational' tag was left off MPAQT and BEACON because the abstracts do not say whether new wet-lab data were generated.
No example posts or example reports were present in the data files, so nothing was deleted for that step.
